newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI sets 1997/98 M3 growth at 15-15.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: India RBI sets 1997/98 M3 growth at 15-15.5 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Tuesday it was targeting M3 money supply growth at between 15 percent and 15.5 percent during fiscal 1997/98 (April-March).

"..monetary policy would seek to maintain the expansion in M3 in the range of 15.0-15.5 percent to keep the inflation rate at around six percent in 1997/98," RBI governor C. Rangarajan said in a statement to chief executives of commercial banks.

The twin objective of the RBI is to contain inflationary pressures without affecting adequate bank credit to support a real gross domestic product growth of 6.0-7.0 percent in 1997/98, he said in a letter to banks spelling out the RBI's credit policy for the first half of 1997/98.
"The projected increase in money supply may be reviewed and revised depending upon macro-economic developments," he said.
